Subject: POC access playmap & activation agenda

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. As promised, I sketched a short playmap for the POC environment activation so we can get Medinova running with Redwood within the two-week pilot window. High level asks below; I attached a draft MAP and a minimal network requirements spreadsheet for your security team.

Quick checklist (target kick-off: Mon Jun 14):
- Org setup: create an admin/owner in your tenant and share the org ID (owner@medinova).
- API keys: we'll provision a read-only test key first and a scoped production key later; procurement needs the PO template attached.
- IP allowlist: please confirm the CIDR blocks your firewall team will allow (see sheet).
- VPC peering: optional for higher throughput — if you want it, we need your VPC ID, peer ASN, and a point-of-contact.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-v1.pdf (PDF, 420KB)], [Attachment: network-requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)]

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm owner email + security contact by EOD Thu (Jun 10).
2) We run a short connectivity validation call (30m) on Mon Jun 14.
3) Exchange API keys and test generator flow by Tue Jun 15.

If procurement needs a PO template to expedite keys, I included that doc too. Happy to move dates by a day or two to match your team's calendar.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: POC access playmap & activation agenda — infra notes

Forwarding Sara's reply with a short infra checklist we should confirm before the connectivity call.

Infra notes (Ben):
- Public endpoint vs peering: if they choose public endpoints, recommend we enable ephemeral token refresh and enforce per-key rate limits to avoid noisy-tenant issues.
- CIDR list: provide both region egress blocks and the option for per-instance IP allowlist (we maintain a stable pool but it can change during maintenance).
- VPC peering data required: VPC ID, region, peer ASN, preferred route tables, and contact for troubleshooting. Peering adds ~1 business day for setup once we have the info and approvals.
- Certificate pinning & mTLS: optional for extra security — we can enable mTLS for the pilot if their infra team requests it.

I also attached a short internal playbook link for the call. Recommend we assign owners and publish the MAP to HubSpot so lifecycle and billing know the pilot is active.

Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal-connectivity-playbook.pdf (PDF, 95KB)]
